video_title: Mo Williams Holds the MOST UNIQUE NBA Record! + Winning Title with 2016 Cavs!

quotes.speaker: Mo Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Mo Williams on coaching his sons at Kentucky and Jackson State
quotes.quote: Well, absolutely. It was a no-brainer for me. But you know, I was a coach at Jackson State obviously for the last four years as a head coach and I had one of my my oldest son was an assistant for me for the last four years and still at Jackson State. And also my son Mike, he's a player at Jackson State. So I was already coaching with my kids and I had the opportunity to take the job here at Kentucky, which was a no-brainer. And obviously now on the floor with Mason on the same same team with him. You know, for me, I just look at it as an opportunity to spend spend time with my kids. Sports bring you closer, bring you together. You're always around your your your your sport family just as much as your family if not more. So I enjoy it. You know, it's a dream come true. It's something that I've always put into fruition and it's always came came about. I was an AAU coach even when I was playing, so I always coached my kids coming up. And I have eight boys.

quotes.speaker: Mo Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Mo Williams on his son Mason's recruitment to Kentucky after initial frustration
quotes.quote: No, so so what happened was my son that that came to me as a freshman, he was a, you know, top 75 kid and he was getting recruited by a lot of schools and what happened was a lot of people were scared to recruit him because they just assumed he was coming to Jackson State to play for me. But that's how he kind of just fell in my lap. And then my other son came up and, you know, he was he kind of fell into the same boat. They were kind of scared to recruit him because they thought he just obviously was going to come play for me. And when when he committed, you know, he got frustrated, committed early, like, I don't want to deal with this. I just come play for you and I wait on you to get another job and we just go somewhere else. So we kind of had that conversation. And, um, so what happened was, um, he was committed. They played against the number one team in the in the country and he went out there and had like 28 and eight and eight, some some crazy stat line and they beat them. Then all of a sudden, like 10 schools called my phone the next day. Hey, are you sure he going to Jackson State? I know he's committed. You know, so I had a conversation with him and I said, listen, you got to decomit. And we decomitted like 48 hours later and just kind of opened his recruitment back up and a lot of schools came into the to the fold and Kentucky was one of them. And, um, I'm glad it worked out for him.

quotes.speaker: Mo Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Mo Williams on leaving head coaching to pursue a national championship at Kentucky
quotes.quote: Absolutely. I mean, obviously we still got a couple more spots to fill. Man, it's like for me, all right, I'll answer. I'll answer your question, but I I have to say this. So for me, um, I was a head coach for the last six years. And being a head coach, you know, you're able to run your program, you're able to recruit. Now, I was at an HBCU, so I paid it forward. Um, just had being in that space, um, having a name and being in that space, a lot of guys don't do that. So I'm I'm I'm grateful for that. Um, but at the same time, we're we're competitive and we want to be in a position to compete for a national championship. So for me, that was my decision to leave a head coaching opportunity to come and be an assistant coach at Kentucky to build something special, to have an opportunity to win a national championship, which we have all the resources in the world to accomplish those goals. So it's going out and being doing what I do best is able to go out and get in homes and and recruit the best players and obviously at the end of the day, develop them and get them to the level that they want to get to and ultimately that's to play at the level we played at for a number of years. Now correct y'all, I played 13, but I was paid 14. So I just wanted to throw that in there.

quotes.speaker: Mo Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Mo Williams on his prime years playing with LeBron James in Cleveland
quotes.quote: He was young and he was and he was still learning, but he was still really good. You know, I I enjoyed like them were some of the best years of my career. You know, it was kind of the beginning of my prime years per se. Everything just came so easy to me at the time playing with LeBron. It it just everything opened up. It it was it was easy. I just wish I was a little bit more focused during the during the offseason during those years. I got complacent. You know, I I think my I think I had a higher floor I could have gotten to. But I think I think it was like a three-year offseason span where we were going to the playoffs and playing 100 games and, you know, them three months I took two and a half of them off. You know, so I I think I think I think if I had a different mindset, which that's why I'm a coach. That's why I help kids and get them to understand like, hey, yeah, you played, but I could have been better. I could have did some more things. I scored 11,000 points and 5,000 assists and All-Star, but I could have done more, I felt like.

quotes.speaker: Mo Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Mo Williams on LeBron James's exceptional preparation
quotes.quote: Well, preparation. Obviously, I was I was playing a lot at that time. Obviously, I was kind of the second option at that time. So, you know, during right before shootaround, I'm going to get my own workout in before we get on the bus and go. So I got to do a little bit more extra to be ready. You know, it was just the offseason I wasn't preparing myself, but during the season, I was locked in. So I'll walk downstairs to get on the treadmill or give me a light workout in before shootaround. He's finishing up. You know, he's already at the gym. When we get on the bus and get to the gym, he's already finished out a workout. Go through shootaround with us. Then we get back to the hotel, first bus at 5, 5:15 or whatever the case. He's leaving at 3:30. He already worked out by the time we get there, start warming up, he on the table getting getting his body worked on. He was doing this, you know, 20 years ago.

quotes.speaker: Mo Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Mo Williams on the fun and connection of the 'Lob City' Clippers team
quotes.quote: So so obviously when I was with Cleveland with LeBron, you know, that was kind of like the the time of my career where I kind of blew up for just who I was just because I'm on TV a lot. But when I went to when I left, I went from one of the most miserable years of my career to one of the most happiest times of my life. Now, before that, I'm in Utah, Milwaukee, Cleveland. And then my next city is LA. So, Lou, you know what I mean? You know exactly what I mean. So I'm like, hold up, I'm going to LA. All right. And the the great thing about it was I had an option to go to it was either the Lakers or the Clippers. So I had two options. And I chose the Clippers. So when I went to to LA and got around that group, so that group was young. You know, DJ was young, Blake was young, which I call Austin. Um, so with that group, I was still young. I was 26, 27 at the time. We hung together all the time. Like we were around each other a lot. We kicked it a lot. Blake used to come to my crib in San Diego because it was two hours away. So at the end of the day, like that that group was real connected. And it showed on the court. It showed on the court and DJ and Blake, they were so young. You just you saw them highlights, man. Just throw the ball in the air. They're going to get it. So it was fun. It was fun. And we were loaded too. People don't realize and obviously when I got there, it was it was right after the lockout. Then CP came. So just imagine this group. This right before Jamal Crawford. So I when I left, they just brought in J-Craw. So it was CP, Caron Butler, Big Shot, uh, Blake, DJ. Then after that, you had myself, Nick Young, Caron Butler, uh, Eric Bledsoe, Reggie Evans, Kenyon Martin. Come on, man. We had no expectations, right? They didn't expect us to do nothing. So it was like a show on the road because time we land, everybody on the bus, hey, what we doing? What we doing? What's and we just go to the game and we 10 deep during the game. We're going to go out there and take care of business. So, all right, you ain't got it tonight. All right, bet. You ain't got it tonight. All right, bet. It was a fun team because we were so connected. It ain't nothing like being on a team that's connected.

quotes.speaker: Mo Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Mo Williams on his unique achievement of winning Player of the Month in both conferences
quotes.quote: So long story short, I ended up going to Charlotte. So my first week in Charlotte, I averaged 30 and eight the first week and won Eastern Conference player of the of the of the, uh, month or week or whatever the case may be. Month. So if you do if you do your research, I might be the only person that has won Eastern Conference and Western Conference player of the month in the same season.

quotes.speaker: Mo Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Mo Williams on staying ready and playing in Games 5, 6, and 7 of the 2016 Finals
quotes.quote: Now we're in the finals. I don't play game one, two, three, or four. We're down 3-1. Now, mind you, T-Lue still ain't came to me and said nothing. So I'm still preparing like I want to prepare. So at this time, I'm already coaching. I don't sit on the bench. I'm all the way at the end on one knee because I got to I got to stand up and down the whole game because I'm coaching. So I'm just down at the end on one knee. And Kyrie, um, that that he either coming out three minutes ago in the first or start of the second. He played the whole first quarter. And all I heard was game five, Mo. Man, I sprinted so fast to the, uh, to the check-in. I'm in ready. And if y'all take the time and go look at those stats, those three games, I was solid. I knew my matchup. I knew what I was supposed to do. Get in. I'm two for three from the field. The one of the floaters y'all saw was in the finals. You know, and I played in game five, six, and seven. Those backup minutes. And I use this story to tell kids like you got to always stay ready. Everything ain't going to go in your favor, but you got to stay ready. Don't mess your life up feeling sorry for yourself that nobody else will. You got to stay down and stay ready. So that was that's a that's a memory that I have from from that from that championship season. Something that I.
